Remark
[Euclidean rigidity outside a compact set]

Source: petersen:page-0374 ↗ thm:pet-ch9-bochner-vanishing-1forms 1. ch9:9.6.6Suppose $M^n-K\cong \mathbb R^n-C$ isometrically for compact $K\subset M$ and $C\subset \mathbb R^n$. Prove that $\operatorname {Ric}_g\ge 0$ forces $(M,g)$ to be Euclidean. One may either embed a neighborhood of $K$ into a metric on $T^n$ that is flat elsewhere, or extend parallel one-forms from $\mathbb R^n-C$ harmonically and apply Bochner vanishing.
